serpGaps: No ranking page gives a weighted scorecard a buyer can actually fill in to compare 3 agencies side by side.
Ranking pages talk about 'process' in general; none show how to test recruitment quality (sample screener, no-show policy, fraud checks, who pays incentives).
Nobody explains how to normalise proposals so prices compare like for like (user groups x participants x methods x recruitment difficulty x readout).
Contract and data terms are missing: who owns recordings, PII retention, consent forms, HIPAA BAA for health products.
No page tells the buyer to request a redacted sample readout and what traceability (evidence to insight to recommendation) looks like.
Most ranking pages are written by design agencies about design agencies; research-specific criteria (dedicated researchers, synthesis method, repository handover) are thin.
No page describes what the first 2 weeks after signing should look like, so buyers cannot judge a slow start.

outline.h2: What decision should the UX research answer before you contact any agency?
outline.answerHint: Start from the product decision (build, kill, redesign, enter a market), not from a method list; an agency can only be judged against a clear decision.
points: Scenario intro continues: a PM with a board deadline and three agency pitches that all list the same methods.
Write the decision as 1 sentence, plus the user groups and the deadline.
Generative vs evaluative: which one the decision needs (one line each, link up to the hub early with anchor 'UX research services').
Why method-first briefs produce proposals you cannot compare.

outline.h2: How do you write a research brief agencies can quote against?
outline.answerHint: A 1-page brief with 6 fields (decision, users, what you already know, constraints, timeline, budget band) gets comparable proposals.
points: Downloadable 1-page brief template (visual: checklist graphic).
Share existing analytics, support tickets and past studies so the agency does not re-buy known answers.
State a budget band; explain why hiding it wastes a round of proposals.
When a formal request for proposal (RFP) helps (procurement, public sector) and when a brief plus a call is enough; cite the GOV.UK user research blog on working with agencies.

outline.h2: Which 7 criteria separate a research agency from a design shop that also does research?
outline.answerHint: Score each agency 1 to 5 on dedicated researchers, method fit, recruitment ownership, synthesis rigor, readout quality, data ethics and domain experience.
points: Weighted scorecard table with suggested weights (visual: scorecard graphic, original design).
Dedicated researchers: ask for names and roles of who runs sessions.
Method fit: did they challenge your method list against your decision (partner vs vendor in our own words).
Domain experience: B2B SaaS and healthcare users behave differently; ask for a similar study, not a similar logo.

outline.h2: How do you test an agency's participant recruitment?
outline.answerHint: Ask for a sample screener, the recruitment channel, the no-show policy and who pays incentives; recruitment quality decides research quality.
points: Panel vs your customer list vs specialist recruiter: trade-offs in 1 short table.
Hard-to-recruit groups (clinicians, warehouse operators, finance admins) and realistic lead times.
Fraud and fit checks: screener logic, live verification, over-recruiting by 1-2 per group.
Participant counts: 10-15 interviews per user group (our standard) and 5 users per qualitative usability round, citing Nielsen Norman Group.

outline.h2: What should a sample research readout show you?
outline.answerHint: A redacted readout should trace every recommendation back to observed evidence and rank findings by impact on the decision.
points: Ask for a redacted readout, not a portfolio case study.
Traceability check: quote or clip -> insight -> recommendation -> owner.
Deliverables that outlive the project: tagged repository (for example in Dovetail), personas, journey maps, opportunity map.
DOWN link: toolsgroup-supply-chain-ux case study (30+ stakeholder interviews reframed product strategy) as an example of a finding that changed a roadmap. Use only facts from the case study file.

outline.h2: 12 questions to ask on the pitch call (and what a strong answer sounds like)
outline.answerHint: Ask about the people, the method choice, recruitment, synthesis, readout and data handling; strong answers are specific to your product.
points: Two-column list: question | what a strong answer includes (original wording, grouped by People, Method, Recruitment, Synthesis, Delivery, Data).
Example: 'Who will moderate the sessions, and can I meet them before we sign?'
Example: 'What would make you recommend fewer interviews than I asked for?'
Natural invitation: we answer these 12 on a first call.

outline.h2: Red flags that mean you should walk away
outline.answerHint: Walk away when an agency agrees to every method you list, cannot name its researchers, sells deliverable counts instead of answers, or has no consent and data plan.
points: 6 red flags, each with the question that exposes it.
Recommendations before any user has been interviewed.
Research presented only as a phase inside a design retainer with no separate plan.
Vague recruitment ('we have a panel') with no screener sample.

outline.h2: How do you compare two research proposals on price and scope?
outline.answerHint: Normalise every proposal to the same 5 units (user groups, participants, methods, recruitment difficulty, readout) before comparing price.
points: Comparison table graphic: proposal A vs B normalised (hypothetical, clearly labelled as an example, no invented market data).
Fixed-fee vs time-and-materials for research; where scope creep hides (extra rounds, re-recruiting, translation).
Our own programme range: $25,000-$60,000 over 4-8 weeks (from the hub); link to the hub's pricing for the full price breakdown instead of repeating it. Do not turn this section into a cost guide.
What a cheap proposal usually leaves out (recruitment, synthesis days, readout).

outline.h2: Which contract terms protect your research data and IP?
outline.answerHint: The statement of work (SOW) should state who owns recordings and findings, how personally identifiable information (PII) is stored and deleted, and how consent is collected.
points: Ownership of raw recordings, transcripts and the repository at handover.
Consent forms and participant rights; cite the Insights Association Code of Standards.

Health products: a HIPAA business associate agreement (BAA) when sessions can expose protected health information; cite the HHS sample BAA provisions (they include return or destruction of PHI at contract end).
Retention and deletion dates, NDA for participants viewing unreleased designs.

outline.h2: What should the first 2 weeks look like after you sign?
outline.answerHint: In the first 2 weeks a good agency agrees research questions, finalises the screener, starts recruitment and books the first sessions.
points: Process diagram: kickoff -> research plan sign-off -> screener live -> first sessions booked -> stakeholder observation invites.
What you owe the agency (access, customer list, a decision owner).
Lead moment: this is where the reader wants the service. Offer: send your 1-page brief and receive a scoped research plan and fixed price you can score with this guide.
Second UP link to the hub near the end; mention our process follows ISO 9241-210 human-centred design.

faqs.q: How many UX research agencies should I shortlist?
faqs.hint: 3 is enough to compare; more than 5 slows the decision. Our recommendation, not a statistic.

faqs.q: Should the UX research agency also do the design?
faqs.hint: Not required; the benefit is continuity of insight, the risk is research bent to justify design. Ask how findings are kept independent.

faqs.q: Do I need an RFP to hire a UX research agency?
faqs.hint: No. A 1-page brief plus a call works for most teams; an RFP is needed when procurement rules require it.

faqs.q: Who owns the recordings from a UX research study?
faqs.hint: Whoever the SOW says; insist the client owns recordings, transcripts and the repository, within participant consent terms.

faqs.q: How fast can a UX research agency start fieldwork?
faqs.hint: Recruitment drives start time; our process puts recruitment at 3-6 days after framing (hub). Hard-to-recruit groups take longer.
